newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to seek up to $1.8 bln abroad in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to seek up to $1.8 bln abroad in 1997.

text.p: The Colombian government said Wednesday that it planned to raise up to $750 million in financing through a 30-year bond issue in the United States next year.

The bond issue would be the centerpiece of the central government's plan to tap foreign markets for up to $1.8 billion in fresh financing in the coming year, a statement from the National Council on Economic and Social Policy (CONPES) said.

The CONPES, comprised by senior economic cabinet officials, the director of the National Planning Department and the head of the country's autonomous central bank, agreed on the $1.8 billion ceiling on new indebtedness in 1997 during a closed-door meeting at the presidential palace early Wednesday.
Colombia issued a 20-year $200 million Yankee bond last February. But the 30-year sovereign debt issue planned for next year would mark Colombia's longest-maturity bond issue yet.
The CONPES statement said the government planned the issuance in the United States because of "yield curve behavior, liquidity and demand for Colombian paper" in the U.S. market.
The Colombian government floated $1.4 billion in bonds on international capital markets this year including a $400 million "Eurodollar" issue in June and a 275 million Deutsche Mark issue last month.
In addition to new bond issues, the CONPES statement said the government had been authorized to meet its foreign debt limit in 1997 through syndicated loans.
